jobs.text: Dhaka grew around the Buriganga river, which carried boats, traders and goods. The Mughals made it a provincial capital in 1610, and it became the capital of an independent Bangladesh in 1971. More than twenty million people now live in greater Dhaka, and the river that built the city is struggling with pollution.

jobs.text: The government of Pakistan had declared Urdu the only state language, although most of its people spoke Bangla. On 21 February 1952 students defied a ban on gatherings near Dhaka University. Police opened fire, and several young men were killed, among them Abul Barkat, Rafiquddin Ahmed, Abdul Jabbar and Abdus Salam. Bangla was recognised as a state language in 1956, and in 1999 UNESCO named 21 February International Mother Language Day.
jobs.alt: The government of Pakistan had declared Urdu the only state language, although most of its people spoke Bangla.

jobs.text: Ready-made garments grew from a handful of factories in the late 1970s into the country’s largest export industry, bringing in around four-fifths of export earnings. Millions of workers, most of them women, stitch clothes for shops around the world. The industry has lifted many families out of poverty, but the collapse of the Rana Plaza building in 2013, which killed more than 1,100 people, led to strong demands for safer factories.
